findings.explanation: The resource has a commented-out `log_config { enable = true }` block (lines 154-156). Cross-checking the actual hashicorp/google provider schema (v7.37.0) shows google_compute_security_policy has no `log_config` block at all -- only adaptive_protection_config, advanced_options_config, recaptcha_options_config, rule, and timeouts. `log_config` exists on google_compute_backend_service (access logging), not on the Cloud Armor policy resource. A previously-generated holden policy (HLD_PROPOSED_008) was authored against this same incorrect path (log_config.enable), so on every scan it neither passes nor fails for this resource -- it is silently skipped (the scan reports Skipped: 3). The policy is dead code that creates a false sense of logging coverage, and the developer's commented-out block would fail to apply with a 'no such attribute' error if uncommented as-is.
findings.remediation: Delete the dead log_config comment block (lines 154-156). Fix or retire HLD_PROPOSED_008 in .holden/policies/ -- see suggested_policies for the corrected check, which targets the resource that actually has an on/off logging switch (google_compute_backend_service.log_config.enable).
findings.title: Custom policy HLD_PROPOSED_008 checks a path that does not exist on google_compute_security_policy, so it silently never fires

findings.explanation: var.log_level's description says 'NORMAL logs matched rules only. VERBOSE logs all evaluated rules', which reads as if this module's setting determines whether Cloud Armor decisions are logged at all. In the actual provider schema, advanced_options_config.log_level only tunes verbosity of an already-logging pipeline; whether Cloud Armor enforcement data is captured at all is gated by log_config.enable on the google_compute_backend_service that the policy is attached to (see outputs.tf's policy_self_link, intended for exactly that attachment). This module never creates a backend service and never asserts or documents that requirement, so a consumer who sets log_level = "VERBOSE" (as example/examplea/module.cloudarmour.tf:61 does) can reasonably believe Cloud Armor is logging when, without log_config.enable = true on their backend service, nothing is recorded. No deterministic rule can catch this because it spans a resource this module doesn't create.
findings.remediation: Add a README/variable-description note that log_level only controls verbosity, and that the consuming google_compute_backend_service must set log_config { enable = true } for any Cloud Armor logs to be produced. Consider adding a backend_service example showing both wired together.
findings.title: log_level variable and README imply this module controls Cloud Armor logging, but the real on/off switch lives on the consumer's backend service

suggested_policies.rationale: google_compute_backend_service has a genuine on/off switch for Cloud Armor / access logging at log_config.enable (confirmed in the hashicorp/google v7.37.0 schema: log_config block with enable, optional_fields, optional_mode, sample_rate attributes). coverage_by_type['google_compute_backend_service'] only contains HLD_GCP_050 (security policy attachment) -- no existing policy checks logging on this resource type. This is the correct replacement for the broken HLD_PROPOSED_008, which checked a non-existent attribute on the wrong resource.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_009
name: GCP backend services must enable access logging
principle: logging-and-monitoring
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  Cloud Armor security policy enforcement decisions (allow/deny, matched rule,
  CVE canary hits) are only captured when the backend service the policy is
  attached to has access logging enabled. Without log_config.enable = true on
  the backend service, WAF and rate-limit decisions are invisible -- there is
  no record of blocked attacks, allowlist hits, or canary triggers, making
  post-incident investigation and rule tuning impossible.
remediation: |
  Add a log_config block to the backend service:

  ```hcl
  resource "google_compute_backend_service" "example" {
    log_config {
      enable      = true
      sample_rate = 1.0
    }
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_compute_backend_service:
    path: log_config.enable
    equals: true
